title: "Assignment 1"

## Description

On April 1, 2025, the federal carbon charge on fuel was set to zero, and
British Columbia ended its own carbon tax on the same day. Quebec, which
prices carbon through cap-and-trade instead, was unaffected. In this
assignment you will use Statistics Canada data on gasoline prices to
measure how much of the tax cut reached drivers at the pump, and use
that measurement to work out who bore the carbon tax.

The assignment is designed to give you practice analysing data in R and
writing up your results in Quarto, and to show how economists use a
change in policy to measure the incidence of a tax.

**Due: Friday, October 9, 2026 at 9:00pm.**

## Instructions

The questions are in the Quarto document above. Open it in RStudio and
press **Render** before you change anything: it should produce a PDF. If
it does not, fix that first, using the [Introduction to R and
Quarto](/content/introtor.qmd) page.

Then work through the questions, writing your R code in the chunks
provided and your answers in the text below each question. The hints
under each question point to sections of the [Introduction to R and
Quarto](/content/introtor.qmd) page, which has a worked example of each
step. Wherever a
written answer is needed, the question has a **Comment on the results**
prompt, just above the answer space, that says what to cover. Tables must
be made with `modelsummary()`, `datasummary()` or `datasummary_df()`,
and graphs must have readable axis labels. Do not copy and paste, or
screenshot, console output.

::: callout-warning
## Some of your answers are marked by computer

Several questions ask you to store a result under a particular name,
such as `q2` or `pt_naive`. Those objects are checked automatically, so:

-   use exactly the names given in the question;
-   do not change the code in the `setup` and `load-data` chunks;
-   do not round the numbers you store (round only when displaying them).

The last chunk in the document tells you whether any of the required
objects are missing.
:::

## The data

The data come from Statistics Canada's monthly survey of retail
gasoline prices, [Table
18-10-0001-01](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/t1/tbl1/en/tv.action?pid=1810000101).
They are the average price of regular unleaded gasoline at self-service
stations in 15 cities, for each month from October 2024 to September
2025: six months before the carbon tax was removed and six months
after, 180 rows in all.

| Variable | Description |
|:-----------|:-----------------------------------------------------------|
| `city` | City |
| `province` | Province |
| `date` | The month, stored as a date (the first day of the month) |
| `month` | The month, as text, such as "2025-03" for March 2025 |
| `gas` | Average price of regular gasoline, in cents per litre, including all taxes |
| `salestax` | The GST or HST rate charged on gasoline in the province (plus the QST in Quebec), as a proportion: 0.13 means 13% |

Three cities in the Statistics Canada table are left out on purpose:

-   **Winnipeg**, because Manitoba's gas tax holiday ended on January 1,
    2025, adding 12.5 cents a litre of provincial tax in the middle of
    the period, for reasons that have nothing to do with the carbon
    tax.
-   **Whitehorse and Yellowknife**, because prices in the territories
    come from few stations and often do not change for months at a time.

One city that is kept has a second change to account for: **Halifax**,
where the HST also fell from 15% to 14% on April 1, 2025. That lowered
the price there by about one more cent.

Source: Statistics Canada, Table 18-10-0001-01, Monthly average retail
prices for gasoline and fuel oil, by geography, October 2024 to
September 2025. Reproduced and distributed on an "as is" basis with the
permission of Statistics Canada.

## Submission

Submit two files on Gradescope, both by the due date:

1.  **Your `.qmd` file**, to the assignment called **Assignment 1 -
    Code**. This is the file that is marked by computer.
2.  **The PDF produced by rendering it**, to the assignment called
    **Assignment 1 - Written**. When you upload it, match each question
    to the page it is on. Your tables, graphs, and written answers are
    marked from this file.

Results from the computer marking are released after the due date, not
when you submit, so use the check at the end of the document before you
submit.

A document that does not render cannot produce a PDF, so render after
every question, not only at the end.

## Marking

The assignment is marked out of 30.

-   **Each of the five questions is marked out of 5** from your PDF,
    using the rubric below. The mark reflects the whole answer: code,
    tables, graphs, and writing.
-   **Your code is marked out of 5 by computer**, from how many of the
    objects you were asked to create are correct.

| Points | Rubric                                                                                            |
|:------:|:--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|   5    | Fully correct                                                                                     |
|   4    | Mostly correct with a minor mistake, or slightly lacking detail                                  |
|   3    | Mostly correct with multiple minor mistakes, a more substantial mistake, or a more significant lack of detail |
|   2    | Mostly incorrect with a major mistake or several minor mistakes                                  |
|   1    | Mostly incorrect with multiple major and minor mistakes                                           |
|   0    | Blank or entirely incorrect                                                                       |

## Generative AI

You may use generative AI for this assignment, but you must say how you
used it. The document has a section at the end for this. Failing to
disclose its use is academic misconduct.

## Plagiarism

This is an independent assignment, which I expect you to complete on
your own. It is plagiarism to copy someone else's work verbatim, which
includes R code. Any work you submit should be yours only. However, you
are encouraged to talk to each other to try to figure out how to do the
assignment.
